source.title: Neural Networks Learn Statistics of Increasing Complexity
source.authors: Nora Belrose; Quintin Pope; Lucia Quirke; Alex Troy Mallen; Xiaoli Z. Fern

page_placements.theme: Unigram/bigram (no-context) stages and plateaus before in-context mechanisms

record.tranche_reason: Measures token-position loss as an indicator of in-context learning in Pythia, a different and partial test of the in-context-learning component of V2. It does not detect induction heads or test their formation.
record.gate_note: The study reports synthetic n-gram sequence-loss curves and token-position loss. It does not measure induction heads, their mechanism, or their formation time. Its n-gram sequence-loss curves are evaluation losses, not the training-loss bump in V2; those curves are not recorded as rows for that claim.
record.test_reason: The study tests the distributional simplicity bias. It borrows Olsson et al.'s token-position criterion for in-context learning (ICL) as a tool to explain why n-gram sequence loss recovers late in training. It never detects, ablates or times induction heads. Its ICL measure uses synthetic maximum-entropy n-gram sequences, not natural text, and covers only six Pythia-12B checkpoints (16, 256, 1,000, 8,000, 66,000, 143,000). That spacing cannot resolve an abrupt onset, a narrow window, or a coincident training-loss bump. So its results do not bear on V2 or any other version. The record's T2 'tests V2' reading overreaches.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that networks learn input statistics in increasing order, supporting the distributional simplicity bias (DSB). Pythia models show double descent on unigram and bigram sequences, with the late recovery hypothesized to be driven by ICL. They describe the ICL link as correlational evidence from Pythia 12B (Fig. 7), not a demonstrated mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Measures token-position loss on synthetic n-gram sequences; does not identify or intervene on induction heads.
record.method_sensitivity: The ICL result differs by evaluation sequence order: some unigram ICL appears by step 1,000 and more after step 8,000, while bigram ICL is reported after step 8,000.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia 12B, loss decreasing with token index on maximum-entropy n-gram sequences appears late. For bigram sequences it appears after step 8,000; for unigram sequences some appears by step 1,000, with more after 8,000. The authors say it correlates with the end of a non-monotonic ('double descent') regime in n-gram sequence loss across Pythia sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LMs' late-training recovery on low-order n-gram sequences is driven by ICL emerging around the end of the non-monotonic loss regime (correlational, Pythia 12B only).

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235 (2024)
record.problems: No induction heads are measured, so the study cannot establish their formation or link their timing to ICL. The token-position result is reported for Pythia 12B on synthetic n-gram sequences and is described qualitatively; no uncertainty estimate is stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant token-position results are stated in the text. Figure 6 and related n-gram sequence-loss curves are evaluation losses, not the training-loss bump specified in V2.

untested.parts: All: no previous-token or induction-head circuit analysis.
All: no induction-head detection, no abruptness test (six checkpoints), no training-loss bump.
All: no attribution of ICL to any heads.
All: no induction behaviour measured across models.
All. Seed and LR-warmup comparisons concern n-gram sequence loss, not induction heads or ICL persistence.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 limits_scope label is dropped. A version can only get a verdict if the study tests it, and this study measures neither induction heads nor phase-change sharpness. The paper's ICL is measured off-distribution, on synthetic maximum-entropy sequences, so even its ICL timing is not comparable to Olsson et al.'s ICL score on natural text. The main contribution is image-classifier and n-gram DSB evidence, unrelated to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Induction-head formation, composition with a previous-token head, and copying behavior.
Induction-head appearance and whether it coincides with the measured ICL onset; the training-loss bump.
Whether induction heads carry most ICL in large transformers.
Induction behavior across model families, architectures, or modalities.

Whether induction-head formation or ICL persistence depends on training-data properties or training setup. The study varies evaluation sequences and reports a warmup comparison, but does not test induction heads or vary the training data.
Whether few-shot task learning is carried mainly by mechanisms other than induction heads.
Whether induction-head formation consists of separate sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: Pythia 12B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated cross-entropy loss by token position on maximum-entropy unigram sequences at six training checkpoints.

conditions.value: six training steps; exact steps not stated here

rows.measure: Cross-entropy loss over successive token positions; decreasing loss at later positions is the study's ICL criterion.
rows.baseline: Loss is uniform across token positions in early training steps.
rows.value: Some ICL is present by step 1,000, with more after step 8,000; loss decreases at later token positions.
rows.note: The authors describe the decrease as developing slowly. This measures ICL, not induction-head formation or its relation to the onset.
rows.check: Measures ICL on synthetic unigram sequences at six sparse checkpoints, with no induction-head measure and no training-loss bump. It cannot show the abrupt, coincident phase change V2 names. Value is read qualitatively from Fig. 7 and text.

rows.subject: Pythia 12B

conditions.value: six training steps; exact steps not stated here

rows.measure: Cross-entropy loss over successive token positions; decreasing loss at later positions is the study's ICL criterion.

rows.value: In-context learning of the maximum-entropy bigram sequence occurs after step 8,000.
rows.note: The study does not report an induction-head measurement at this step or test whether the ICL change is abrupt.
rows.check: Same issue as R1, for bigram sequences. 'After step 8,000' is bounded only by checkpoints 8,000 and 66,000, so onset timing and sharpness cannot be read.

relation.reason: Applies the ICL criterion cited to Olsson et al. without detecting, intervening on, or timing induction heads.

tranche.reason: Uses the cited token-position ICL criterion to interpret n-gram prediction results; does not measure induction heads or test any claim version.

source_check.notes: Figure 7 checkpoints are 16, 256, 1,000, 8,000, 66,000 and 143,000 steps. These sparse behavioral measurements cannot establish abrupt induction-head formation; the link between ICL and late loss recovery is correlational.
